questions.stem: A cube is rotated 90 degrees around an axis passing through its center and parallel to one of its faces. Which face will now be facing upwards?

choices.A: The face opposite to the starting face.
choices.B: The same face as the starting face.
choices.C: A face adjacent to the starting face.

questions.solution: When a cube is rotated 90 degrees around an axis passing through its center and parallel to one of its faces, it will effectively 'flip' over that face. So, the face opposite the starting face will now be facing upwards.
questions.explanation: This question tests understanding of rotations about axes other than the principal axes of a cube.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose option B (the same face as the starting face), which might happen if the student assumes that the rotation doesn't change the orientation of the faces.

questions.stem: A rectangular prism is rotated 180 degrees around an axis passing through its center and perpendicular to its length. Which dimension will now be facing opposite its original position?
questions.solution: When a rectangular prism is rotated 180 degrees around an axis perpendicular to its length, the height dimension will face opposite its original position.
questions.explanation: This question tests understanding of rotations about axes other than the principal axes of a rectangular prism.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose option A (length), which might happen if the student incorrectly assumes that the rotation affects the length dimension.

questions.stem: A cylinder is rotated 45 degrees around an axis passing through its center and perpendicular to its height. Which of the following best describes the new orientation?

choices.A: The base and top are now at a 45-degree angle with respect to their original position.
choices.B: The base and top remain parallel to their original position.
choices.C: The base and top are now perpendicular to their original position.

questions.solution: When a cylinder is rotated 45 degrees around an axis perpendicular to its height, the base and top will be at a 45-degree angle with respect to their original position.
questions.explanation: This question tests understanding of rotations about axes other than the principal axes of a cylinder.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose option B (the base and top remain parallel), which might happen if the student misunderstands how a rotation affects the orientation of the cylinder.

questions.stem: A cone is rotated 360 degrees around an axis passing through its apex and perpendicular to its base. Which face will now be facing downwards?

choices.C: The same face as the starting position.

questions.solution: When a cone is rotated 360 degrees around an axis passing through its apex and perpendicular to its base, it returns to its original orientation; thus, the base will still be facing downwards.
questions.explanation: This question tests understanding of rotations about axes other than the principal axes of a cone.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose option C (the same face as the starting position), which might happen if the student forgets that a full rotation brings the object back to its original orientation.

questions.stem: A tetrahedron is rotated 90 degrees around an axis passing through one vertex and perpendicular to the opposite face. Which vertex will now be in the position of the starting vertex?

choices.C: The same vertex as the starting vertex.

questions.solution: When a tetrahedron is rotated 90 degrees around an axis passing through one vertex and perpendicular to the opposite face, an adjacent vertex will be in the position of the starting vertex.
questions.explanation: This question tests understanding of rotations about axes other than the principal axes of a tetrahedron.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose option C (the same vertex as the starting vertex), which might happen if the student misunderstands how a rotation affects the positions of vertices in a tetrahedron.

questions.stem: A sphere is rotated 120 degrees around an axis passing through its center and intersecting two diametrically opposite points on its surface. Which point will now be at the highest position?

choices.B: A point on the same great circle as the starting point, but 120 degrees away.
choices.C: A point diametrically opposite to the starting point.

questions.solution: When a sphere is rotated 120 degrees around an axis passing through its center and intersecting two diametrically opposite points, a point on the same great circle as the starting point but 120 degrees away will be at the highest position.
questions.explanation: This question tests understanding of rotations about axes other than the principal axes of a sphere.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose option A (the starting point), which might happen if the student forgets that a rotation moves points along a great circle on the sphere.

questions.stem: A triangular prism is rotated 270 degrees around an axis passing through its center and parallel to one of its lateral edges. Which face will now be facing downwards?

choices.C: The same face as the starting position.

questions.solution: When a triangular prism is rotated 270 degrees around an axis passing through its center and parallel to one of its lateral edges, one of the triangular faces will now be facing downwards.
questions.explanation: This question tests understanding of rotations about axes other than the principal axes of a triangular prism.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose option C (the same face as the starting position), which might happen if the student misunderstands how a rotation affects the orientation of the triangular faces.
